ModifyHandDraw.rationale: PaelsBlood.cs:14-21 returns `count + base.DynamicVars.Cards.IntValue`; CanonicalVars is `new CardsVar(1)` (PaelsBlood.cs:12) with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so 1 is the pinned non-ascension value and paels_blood.py:20's `CARDS = 1` matches. guards.what: N1: `if (player != base.Owner) return count;` (PaelsBlood.cs:16-19) -- the sim's port has no player check at all
guards.rationale: STRUCTURALLY SATISFIED, executed rather than asserted (binding rule 5): `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py blood-draw` enumerates every caller of the hook and finds exactly one outside the dispatcher itself -- player.py:171, `self._hooks.modify_hand_draw(self, self.DRAW_PER_TURN)`, where `self` IS the combat's single PlayerCombatState. The sim's CombatState holds one player by construction, so `player != base.Owner` can never be true and the omitted guard cannot change an outcome. It is a multiplayer-only parameter check, noted in the mapping per the shared contract rather than verdicted as a divergence.

guards.what: N2: the C# hook is a decimal chain and the sim's is an int chain
guards.rationale: Hook.ModifyHandDraw folds `count` through every listener; the sim does the same (hooks.py:219-221) and the relic contributes a whole number, so no rounding can differ. Checked because the three other ported modify_hand_draw listeners are powers (powers.py:2648, :2746, :3895) that also contribute integers, so the fold cannot produce a fractional intermediate that the sim would truncate differently.
